name: fal x Sequoia 72-Hour Video Hack
theme: Generative media and developer tools for AI video
tracks: Generative Media (Film & Animation, Brand & Advertising, Anime, Open)

facts.claim: Hackathon runs July 17–19, 2026; submission deadline July 19 9:00 AM PT
Teams may have up to 4 members
All projects must be new work started during the hackathon
Generative Media Track prohibits third-party IP and non-consensual imitations of real people or copyrighted characters
facts.source: Rules – Generative Media Track Video Submissions

facts.claim: Generative Media Track themes: Film & Animation, Brand & Advertising, Anime, Open
Developer Track requires GitHub repository and a max 3-minute demo video of a tool/workflow for AI-generated video
Each participant receives $100 in fal credits
Judging: GenMedia Track weights – Creative vision/originality/art direction 30%, Storytelling 35%, Technical capability 20%, Effective use of AI 15%
Judging: Developer Track weights – Creativity 25%, User value 25%, Technical execution 35%, Demo 15%

facts.source: Build with fal and Partner Resources

facts.claim: Preview is a collaborative workspace for AI video with $50 credits and supports models from Google, xAI, Kling, ByteDance

inference.claim: The hackathon strongly favors projects that integrate multiple models and demonstrate clever, non-obvious AI pipelines rather than shallow API wrappers
inference.rationale: The Google DeepMind resource guide explicitly warns against 'incremental wrapper apps or basic prompt wrappers,' and the Effective Use of AI criterion rewards pushing tools beyond obvious use.

inference.claim: Sequoia’s sponsorship signals interest in commercially viable, scalable AI-video tools; projects with clear market applicability and polished demos may have an edge in final judging
inference.rationale: Sequoia is a venture capital firm; their hackathon sponsorships typically scout for high-potential startups and investable ideas.

inference.claim: The requirement of fal session logs for Generative Media Track indicates that technical depth and creative prompt workflows will be scrutinized, not just final output
inference.rationale: Submission requirements mandate session logs, which expose the actual tool usage and iteration strategy.

inference.claim: Developer Track projects that reduce friction for creators (editing, consistency, real-time feedback) are likely to score high on User Value
inference.rationale: The track explicitly targets tools that make AI video production faster, easier, or more powerful, aligning with real-world professional pain points.

sanitized_brief: This is the fal x Sequoia 72-Hour Video Hack, July 17–19, 2026, remote. Two tracks: Generative Media (submit a ≤3 min AI-generated video under Film & Animation, Brand & Advertising, Anime, or Open) and Developer (build tools/workflows for AI video, submit GitHub repo + demo video). Team size up to 4, all work must be new. Use $100 fal credits and partner tools — Grok Imagine, Google Gemini, Kling, Preview — via fal API. Submission deadline July 19 9am PT. Prizes: $50k credits + $10k cash. GenMedia judging: story 35%, creative vision/art direction 30%, technical 20%, effective AI use 15%. Developer judging: technical execution 35%, creativity 25%, user value 25%, demo 15%. Strict rules: no third-party IP, no non-consensual likenesses, no explicit content. Do not build basic wrappers, generic chatbots, or simple editors; push beyond obvious model outputs, leverage fal's 1000+ models, workflows, Assets for character consistency, and agent-ready tools to create surprising creative experiences or powerful productivity tools for AI video.
